CIRCUIT: a simple two-loop mesh. Outer rectangle: left column x~190 (top-left corner 190,352 down to V-DC #5 and on to the bottom-left corner 190,625), top rail y~350 carrying the 5k Resistor #0, right column x~665 (top-right corner down through I-DC #4 to the bottom-right corner 665,600), bottom rail y~610..625. A middle rail at y~437 runs from the left column (188,440) through the 2mH Inductor #2 and the 4F Capacitor #1 to the right column (661,430). A middle column drops from the middle rail at (423,442) through the vertical 5k Resistor #3 to the bottom rail at (431,613) and on to the GND symbol #6 at (431,649). 7 components, 4 nets.

NET MAP
  0   = the bottom rail plus ground: bottom terminal of V-DC #5 (187,592), the whole bottom rail y~610-625 from x=190 to x=665, bottom terminal of I-DC #4 (672,567), bottom lead of Resistor #3 (430,586) and GND #6.
  n1  = the left column and everything it feeds: top terminal of V-DC #5 (193,525), up past the middle-rail T at (190,456) to the top-left corner (190,352), east along the top rail to the left lead of Resistor #0 (377,345); and east along the middle rail to the left lead of Inductor #2 (253,453).
  n2  = the right column: right lead of Resistor #0 (487,348), east to the top-right corner (665,348), down past the middle-rail T at (661,430) to the top terminal of I-DC #4 (670,510); the middle rail's right end brings in the right plate of Capacitor #1 (571,437).
  n3  = the centre segment of the middle rail: right lead of Inductor #2 (353,445), left plate of Capacitor #1 (522,438), and the top lead of Resistor #3 (427,500) which hangs down from the T at (423,442).

JUDGEMENT CALLS
  * S18 (431,619) -> JUNCTION. This is the only genuinely contestable site: the vertical run from the bottom of Resistor #3 continues in one unbroken stroke through the bottom rail and down to the GND bar at y~640, so at 8x zoom it reads as a plain 4-way X (the tracer calls it deg=5 because the GND bar's own ends count as branches). There is no solder dot and no hop. I read it as a junction for three reasons: (a) the ink prior - a plain crossing with no hop or jog is a junction in this dataset; (b) drafter habit gives no counter-evidence, because this sheet contains no solder dots at all - every other node on it (S5, S6, S7) is an undotted T, so the absence of a dot here carries no information; (c) the crossing reading is physically odd: it would mean the drafter deliberately routed a wire from the resistor across the bottom rail to a ground symbol while leaving the rail ungrounded, making net 0 just {Resistor #3 bottom, GND} and leaving {V-DC bottom, I-DC bottom} as a separate floating rail with no ground reference. The junction reading - resistor bottom lands on the bottom rail, and the rail is grounded by the GND symbol drawn immediately under that node - is the natural draughting.
  * S5 (661,430), S6 (423,442), S7 (190,456) -> JUNCTION, recorded explicitly. All three are unambiguous deg-3 Ts (a wire terminating on a through-running wire), verified at 8x: S5 is the middle rail's right end landing on the right column, S6 is the middle column starting on the middle rail, S7 is the middle rail's left end landing on the left column. Nothing to decide, but recorded so it is clear they were inspected.
  Non-critical sites S0, S2, S3 (ink of Resistor #0 and its '5KOhm' label), S10 (the '4F' label under the capacitor), S12 (the '2mH' label under the inductor) and S15 (the '5KOhm' label brushing Resistor #3) are all text or symbol ink and change nothing.

PORTS: no fixes needed. Every component's t0/t1 already point at real leads; the flagged 'unused port candidates' on #0 (424,368) and #1 (542,461),(575,461) are strokes of the handwritten '5KOhm' and '4F' labels, and the real leads were already selected. #3's p2@(450,541) is likewise the '5KOhm' text. No 3-terminal parts on this sheet, so no pin-order questions.

CLASSES: all 7 as annotated - Resistor #0 (5k, horizontal, top rail), Capacitor #1 (4F), Inductor #2 (2mH), Resistor #3 (5k, vertical), I-DC #4 (circle with down arrow, 20A), V-DC #5 (circle with battery bars, 20V), GND #6. No overrides.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. All 13 terminals carry a net and ERC is clean.
